h: פָּרָשַׁת כִּי תֵצֵא, י״ב Ki Seitzei, 12
A Moment of Anger and Everlasting Kindness in Exile

p: "Sing, O barren one, who did not bear," etc.,
"for more are the children of the desolate one
than the children of the married one" (Yeshayahu 54:1).
In the new Pesikta (on this haftarah; Pesikta deRav Kahana 20:5):
"She raised up more righteous men in her destruction
she raised up for Me when she was built."
If so, why is she called barren?
who has not borne children for Gehinnom
According to the plain meaning it seems
over the fact that she appears like a barren woman in exile,
that she did not bear children for Gehinnom,
who lived in the time of the Temple.
in the writings of the Arizal,
that he said to his disciple Rabbi Chaim Vital
with intent for the sake of Heaven
than the great deeds they used to do
And this is the meaning of "sing, O barren one":
although it appears to be like a barren woman,
nevertheless "more are the children of the desolate one":
though in truth they are poor in their stature,
because they are the children of the desolate one,
living in this generation, an orphaned generation,
and a small thing is precious
"than the children of the married one"
"For a small moment I forsook you,
and with great compassion I will gather you;
I hid My face from you for a moment,
and with everlasting kindness I have had compassion on you."
First it says "I will gather you,"
and afterward it says "I have had compassion on you,"
The matter is this: it says (Berachos 7a):
One part out of fifty-eight thousand
A moment, as long as it takes to say it."
And the measure of the moment
for nothing at all can be said in it;
and therefore it is called "a small moment."
And this follows what we said
to resolve the question of the Ritva
but did they not say (Bava Basra 99a)
that when they do not do
their faces are toward the House?
not doing the will of the Omnipresent!
that as long as the enemies had not entered,
they did not believe it would be destroyed;
and at the moment they saw that they had entered,
all of Yisrael immediately had thoughts
doers of the will of the Omnipresent;
and therefore the Keruvim were intertwined.
And from this thought of teshuvah
there was then born the spirit of Mashiach,
(in the Yerushalmi and Midrash Eichah; Yerushalmi Berachos 2:4, Eichah Rabbah 1:51)
that on the Ninth of Av Mashiach was born
(and this was explained in Devarim, section 13).
And this is "for a small moment I forsook you":
which is one part out of fifty-eight thousand
But this too was for the good,
so that from it would branch out
"and with great compassion I will gather you,"
"I hid My face from you for a moment";
and here it does not say "a small moment,"
for the little wrath and the hiding of the Face
lasted a moment as long as it takes to say it;
and then, in truth, there was
"and with everlasting kindness I have had compassion on you,"
in the ingathering of Ezra in the Second Temple,
וְאַחַר כָּךְ שָׁלַט בָּהֶם הָאוֹיֵב שֵׁנִית
and afterward the enemy ruled over them again;
And this is the consolation in exile:
for although we have been in exile
already more than eighteen hundred years
and is this a small moment?
that the abandonment was only a small moment,
and the little wrath and the hiding of the Face
a moment as long as it takes to say it;
but it is with everlasting kindness,
so that the redemption be forever,
And even when they are in exile,

p: "For this is to Me as the waters of Noach:
that the exile of Yisrael is reckoned in His eyes
as the destruction of the whole world;
for the whole world was created
only for the sake of Yisrael,
"'In the beginning' — for the sake of Yisrael,
וְזֶהוּ כִּי מֵי נֹחַ זֹאת לִי
and this is "for this is to Me as the waters of Noach."
And it calls it "the waters of Noach"
in line with what they said
that he and his sons would be saved,
he did not beg mercy for the world,
אִקְרוּן מֵי הַמַּבּוּל עַל שְׁמֵיהּ וְכוּלֵּי
the waters of the Flood are called by his name," etc.
But why are the waters of the Flood called
and not mentioned so anywhere else?
רַק הוּא עַל פִּי מַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר (שָׁם נט, טז)
Rather, it follows what is said (Yeshayahu 59:16):
"And He saw that there was no man,
and was astonished that there was no intercessor," etc.
that is, that there should be one man
who would be the individual who repents,
into the heart of the whole community;
and this is "and He saw that there was no man."
"And was astonished that there was no intercessor":
one who would pray for the community.
is one who presses very hard
and says, "I will not move from here
in the name of our holy Rebbe of Izhbitza,
זֵכֶר צַדִּיק וְקָדוֹשׁ לִבְרָכָה לְחַיֵּי הָעוֹלָם הַבָּא
may the memory of the holy tzaddik be a blessing for the life of the World to Come,
And this is "that there was no intercessor,
so His own arm brought Him salvation," etc.
וְזֶה שֶׁאָמַר כִּי מֵי נֹחַ זֹאת לִי וְגוֹ׳
And this is why it says "for this is to Me as the waters of Noach," etc.:
although Noach did not then pray
that the waters of Noach would not pass,"
not to be angry with you, nor to rebuke you."

p: And we have said that the seven consolations
correspond to the seven lower attributes
and if we count the order
corresponds to Yaakov Avinu, peace be upon him.
And they said in the Midrash (on Eichah 2:1; Eichah Rabbah 2:2):
"'He cast down from heaven to earth
here it is, flung in your faces!
כָּךְ אָמַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לְיִשְׂרָאֵל
So the Holy One, Blessed is He, said to Yisrael:
because of the image of Yaakov
that is engraved on My Throne?
Here it is, flung in your faces!" etc.
And about this it says in this haftarah:
I hid My face from you for a moment";
"He cast down from heaven to earth
"and He did not remember His footstool
on the day of His anger";
"For His anger is but a moment,"
for His wrath lasts a moment,
for only "on the day of His anger"
and the glory of Yisrael was restored
And this is "in a little wrath
I hid My face from you for a moment,
and with everlasting kindness I have had compassion on you":
that is, even if one could imagine,
that the merit of the Avos be exhausted,
and the merit of the Imahos,
"My kindness shall not depart from you,
nor shall My covenant of peace totter."
and he merited to be living and enduring,
and from the Angel of Death,
And here, since Hashem Yisbarach gave
a covenant of peace to all of Yisrael,
And although the evil has not yet been nullified
as it will be in the future,
when "He will swallow up death forever" (Yeshayahu 25:8),
is only like sleep and waking.
And every individual soul of Yisrael
who keeps Shabbos according to its halachah
"says Hashem, Who has compassion on you."
